title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's 1986 'Analysis situs' notes axiomatize a 'tame' geometry. A figure F is a subset of an ambient space M given with a decomposition into elementary pieces ('éléments', the set \tilde F, ordered by specialization). F' ≤ F means F' is a sub-figure (a union of strata of F, closed under specialization). G ≪ F means G is a refinement of F. The circled versions (≪ with a ring, ∥ with a ring) are reserved for elementary figures, i.e. elements of the class \mathcal M.

The relation written ≭ (here rendered ≱) is a symmetric 'compatibility' or 'general position' relation between figures. In terms of it:
- F ∥ G ('disjoint and compatible') holds iff every pair of elements x ∈ \tilde F, y ∈ \tilde G satisfies x ∥ y.
- Equivalently, F ≭ G and F ∩ G = ∅.

Proposition 1 (only announced) lists the formal properties of (\mathcal F, ≤): (a) abstractly, and (b) as a family of subsets of M. The margin adds 'including existence of Inf_\mathcal F' when \mathcal F is nonempty.

Proposition 2 ('division' of properties):
- (a) Compatibility passes to sub-figures.
- (b) Compatibility is local. If F = ∪F_i is a Sup of sub-figures, then G ≭ F iff G ≭ F_i for all i. Hence for F = ∪F_i and G = ∪G_j, F ≭ G iff F_i ≭ G_j for all i, j.
- A crossed-out version of (b), 'F ∥ G, F' ≪ F, G' ≪ G ⇒ F' ∥ G'', is postponed. It reappears on the next page as a corollary of Prop. 5 with L = ∅.

Proposition 3 (restriction of a refinement to a sub-figure): given G ≪ F and F' ≤ F, there is a G' with G' ≤ G and G' ≪ F'. Concretely, G' = Inf^{≪}(F', G) and \tilde G' = \tilde G ∩ Omb(F'), where Omb(F') ('shadow') is the set of cells of G lying over F'.
- Notation: G' = G_{F'} = G|F'.
- The map F' ↦ G_{F'} from Sefi_0(F) to Sefi_0(G) is increasing and commutes with arbitrary Sup and Inf. Here Sefi_0 is the lattice of (closed) sub-figures.

Modern reading: a refinement G ≪ F induces a monotone map of strata posets \tilde G → \tilde F. Sub-figures are down-sets, i.e. Alexandrov-closed sets. Restriction is the preimage map, which is a complete lattice homomorphism.

The page sets up the next one, where refinements form a sheaf: Raff(F) = lim_{X ∈ \tilde F} Raff(X), with gluing over coverings F = ∪F_i. This is the foundational, axiomatic part of his tame-topology / stratified-figures program.
errors: No genuine error visible. Prop 2(b) needs F = ∪F_i to be a Sup in the lattice of sub-figures (as stated) and compatibility to be defined elementwise. Both seem intended.

The claim that F' ↦ G_{F'} commutes with arbitrary Sup and Inf presupposes that Sefi_0(F) is a complete lattice and that sub-figures are exactly the unions of strata (down-sets). For infinite families this needs local finiteness or the margin's existence of Inf_\mathcal F. This is flagged in the margin, not proved here.

ideas.what: Disjoint-compatibility F ∥ G defined elementwise, and equivalent to compatibility plus empty intersection
ideas.modern_name: pairwise compatibility / general position of stratifications
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in stratification theory (Whitney, Thom, Mather); o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 sketches tame topology only programmatically

ideas.what: Compatibility is hereditary for sub-figures and local with respect to unions (Prop 2)
Restriction of a refinement G ≪ F to a sub-figure F' ≤ F, given by \tilde G' = \tilde G ∩ Omb(F'); the map F' ↦ G|F' is a complete lattice homomorphism
ideas.modern_name: pullback of Alexandrov-closed sets (down-sets) along the monotone map of strata posets induced by a refinement
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard order theory; stratified spaces as maps to posets (Lurie, Higher Algebra App. A; Ayala-Francis-Tanaka)

ideas.what: Setup for the sheaf property of refinements (next page): Raff(F) = lim_{X ∈ \tilde F} Raff(X)
ideas.modern_name: refinements form a sheaf / stack over the Alexandrov site of the strata poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: implicit in work on refinements of stratifications and exit-path categories; no single standard credit

missed.claim: This page belongs to an unpublished axiomatic foundation of 'tame topology' through figures, refinements (≪), sub-figures (≤), compatibility and the 'shadow' Omb. It frames the theory functorially: restriction of refinements is a lattice homomorphism, and the next page shows refinements glue as a sheaf over the strata poset. This anticipates the now-standard view of stratified spaces as spaces over posets, but the individual results on this page are routine.
missed.quote: F' ↦ G_{F'} : Sefi_0(F) → Sefi_0(G) et croissante et commute aux Sup et aux Inf quelconques.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's concrete 1986 attempt at the tame-topology foundations announced in the Esquisse. It is of historical interest for o-minimal and stratified homotopy theory, though not mathematically new.

deep.surprise_reason: Foundational bookkeeping: elementwise compatibility, its locality, and restriction of refinements as preimage of down-sets. Historically interesting as part of the unpublished tame-topology axiomatics, but each statement is routine.
transcription_corrections: Prop 1: 'a) stratification[?]' is more likely 'a) abstraites' (formal properties abstractly), contrasted with 'b) en tant qu'ensemble de parties de M'.
Prop 2b: 'Sup en son[?] - figure[?]' likely reads 'Sup de sous-figures'.
Left margin: probably 'y inclus l'existence des Sup et ... Inf_𝔉 (𝔉 ≠ ∅)' rather than 'conditions sur'.
Second margin: probably 'prop 1, prop 2 concernent seulement ≤'.
The relation symbol transcribed as ≱ is the same compatibility symbol ≭ used on the previous page.
On the next page, 'Inj^{≪}(G,F')' and 'Inj^{≤}' should read 'Inf^{≪}', 'Inf^{≤}', consistent with G' = Inf^{≪}(F',G) on this page.
